reference_sql:
SELECT e.ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id,
  COALESCE(p.value.int_value, p.value.float_value, p.value.double_value) AS value
FROM events AS e, unnest(e.event_params) AS t(p)
WHERE e.event_name = 'purchase'
  AND e.event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  AND p.key = 'value'
alternatives:
WITH purchases AS (
  -- one row per purchase from 1 to 7 December 2025
  SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'value')[1].value AS v
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
)
SELECT transaction_id, COALESCE(v.int_value, v.float_value, v.double_value) AS value
FROM purchases

SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id, ecommerce.purchase_revenue AS value
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
  AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'

)

other_way.tradeoff: Picking the value parameter with list_filter keeps one row per purchase without a join to the list.
